summary: A playground at Long Bridge and China Basin streets in Mission Bay, part of the Mission Bay Parks system (labeled P6 on OCII's current Mission Bay South open-space page), that opened to the public in 2016 after months of delay; the Urban Life Signs blog, in a post dated June 30, 2016, announced an opening on July 1, 2016 (an announced date, not a confirmed one), while Mission Bay Parks' own post, dated September 15, 2016, says the park is "finally open" and gives no day.

milestones.text: Playground construction visibly complete (grass grown in, play equipment and nature huts installed) but fenced off and not yet open to the public. Urban Life Signs (June 30, 2016) says it "appeared to be completed ... over a year ago" and attributes the closure to "transferring private redeveloped land over to the city"; SFist (May 26, 2016) says work "was finished months ago" and cites Board of Supervisors approval and, in the developer's statement, completion and acceptance of the streets fronting the park (Long Bridge and China Basin)
Mission Bay Kids' Park playground opens to the public

open_questions: Exact opening date is unresolved: the Urban Life Signs blog post, dated June 30, 2016, says the playground "will open July 1, 2016" (an announced date, written before the opening; a photo caption there reads "Last piece being taken away on July 1, 2016"); Mission Bay Parks' own post announcing the opening is dated September 15, 2016 and doesn't state a specific day, raising the possibility of a later or phased opening than the blog's July date -- flagged rather than picked.

Neither source says in its text who designed or built the park; Urban Life Signs credits RHAA as the source of two park images ("Park design. Source: RHAA") but does not call RHAA the designer, and no landscape architect or general contractor is named.

The 2015 under-construction/visibly-finished date is derived from the Urban Life Signs post (published June 2016), which describes the playground as having looked complete, with grass grown in, 'over a year ago' -- an approximate back-calculation, not a directly stated date. A separate SFist article (May 26, 2016, 'Completed Mission Bay Park Fenced Off For Months Due To Red Tape') says "work on the park was finished months ago" and describes a neighbor breaking the lock "on a February day", which implies completion before February 2016 but does not date it. An SF Chronicle article of June 12, 2016 cited earlier could not be located and is not relied on. The sources also give different reasons for the closure: Urban Life Signs says the transfer of redeveloped land to the city; SFist cites Board of Supervisors approval and, in the developer's statement, completing and getting the city's acceptance of Long Bridge and China Basin streets. Neither confirms 2015 versus early 2016; 2015 is used here as the more specific of the two estimates but is flagged as approximate.
